docs.title: Lesson overview
docs.text:
Description This lesson introduces the Odyssey framework, an R Shiny application that supports interactive exploration of biodiversity data. Through hands-on examples, learners will use Odyssey to investigate molecular biodiversity records alongside geographic metadata and gain experience with practical data discovery workflows for biodiversity research and data management.

Prerequisites To be able to follow this course, learners should have knowledge in:  1. Basic familiarity with R and RStudio

Learning Outcomes: By the end of the course, learners will be able to:  1. Use the Odyssey interface to explore biodiversity datasets  2. Inspect and assess geographic and molecular metadata consistency

Target Audience: Researchers, undergraduate students, postgraduate students, citizens scientists, stakeholders, and more.

Level: Beginner to Intermediate

Schedule: This self-paced and self-directed learning module lets you advance at your convenience. Before starting, please install the necessary software. Once set up, feel free to practice with the use cases at your own pace.

Duration: Excluding the initial setup phase, the course content is designed for completion in under an hour.

License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License

Funding: This work was supported by ELIXIR, the research infrastructure for life science data (through the 2024-SCIENCE-BFSP commissioned services project).

docs.title: Data setup
docs.text: No prior data download is required for this lesson. The application is designed to automatically query and retrieve the necessary data directly during runtime. Please just ensure you have an active internet connection to allow the application to fetch the data successfully.

docs.title: Software setup
docs.text: To follow this lesson, learners need a working R environment and RStudio.

docs.title: Required software:
docs.text:
• R (version 4.5 or newer, 4.6 recommended): Download and installation instructions are available from the Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN): https://cran.r-project.org/

  • RStudio RStudio provides an integrated development environment for R and is strongly recommended for this lesson: https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/

docs.title: Mt. Mount Athos (a location based data exploration)
docs.text:
ENA was queried for records from 2020–2025 in the Mount Athos peninsula, revealing 9 sequences of Lathyrus oleraceus - all full plastomes highly informative for phylogenetics and gene-flow studies. Two records with incorrect geographical coordinates were identified and flagged. GBIF data for the same region provided complementary human-observation records, including insect occurrences, enabling spatial comparisons of genetic diversity and species distribution. Please follow this story in the presentation below:

In case your browser does not support PDF rendering, please download the PDF instead.

docs.title: Mt. Voras and Mt. Paiko (a taxon/location based data browsing)
docs.text:
A search for Fagus sylvatica (beech) ENA records in Greece returned only two records lacking geographical coordinates. Thus, these records are shown at the country centre. By cross-referencing the metadata, the actual collection sites on Mt. Paiko and Mt. Voras could be identified, located in one of Europe’s most important glacial refugia. A broader plant query for the area, combined with GBIF-reported insect records, illustrated how Odyssey supports multi-taxon spatial genetic analyses and habitat evaluation. Please follow this story in the presentation below:

In case your browser does not support PDF rendering, please download the PDF instead.

docs.title: Norway’s Ulva (a taxon/location based data exploration)
docs.text:
Searching ENA for plant records along the Norwegian coast (2023–2025) revealed Ulva sp. sequences for the rbcl barcoding marker (Ulva sp are green tubular macroalga common in coastal habitats). GBIF observations for the same area provided additional biotope context. This use case demonstrated how Odyssey supports phylogenetic studies, ecotype identification, and conservation strategy development for coastal species. Please follow this story in the presentation below:

In case your browser does not support PDF rendering, please download the PDF instead.

docs.title: Cretan Sea (a location based data browsing)
docs.text:
A search spanning 2000–2026 in the Cretan Sea returned 40 COI marker gene sequences of Hermodice carunculata (bearded fireworm), two mitochondrial D-loop sequences of Prionace glauca (blue shark), six 16S rRNA sequences of copepods, and one ND1 sequence of Pelophylax cretensis (Cretan frog, an endemic endangered species, incorrect coordinates). GBIF queries for the same region revealed hundreds of human observations for marine fauna, such as perciformes, atheriniformes, and cetaceans. Interactive record filtering via the Odyssey Table tab enabled targeted, taxon-level biodiversity assessment. This functionality allowed records with incorrect geographical coordinates, like certain GBIF-reported plants, to be excluded from the map display.
